tasks.title: Tracer: /pick on GitHub path end to end
tasks.description: New shared skill claude-code-shared/skills/pick/SKILL.md (disable-model-invocation: true, low tier, thin orchestrator, standard learning-capture tail with slug pick). Resolves the repo via the origin remote, looks up its repo-policy.json entry, reads issue_tracker. Repos with no issue_tracker exit cleanly with 'no issue_tracker configured for <repo>'. Adds pick_buckets to the SpawnedSapien entry (pre-launch, opsec, polish, seed-ready with the GitHub search strings and sort arrays from the seed). Bare /pick opens a 'Which bucket?' menu (max 4). scripts/pick/pick-fetch-gh.sh runs the bucket's native gh search and emits normalized candidate JSON. Cheap pre-sort on label tier, then render top 5 with a one-line item and a start line 'wt <branch>  ->  /grill-me #N' where branch is a slug from the issue title. Strictly read-only, terminal output only, no report file. Register pick in model-tiers.json. Add pick_buckets to the repo-policy schema checked by scripts/tests/test-standup-registration.sh if it rejects unknown keys.
acceptance_criteria: Running /pick in a repo without issue_tracker prints 'no issue_tracker configured for <repo>' and exits 0
Running pick-fetch-gh.sh against a recorded gh fixture emits normalized candidate JSON that validates, checked by a smoke script in scripts/tests/
Bare /pick in SpawnedSapien shows a 'Which bucket?' menu with the four configured buckets and prints a top-5 list with start lines
Skill and scripts make no write calls to GitHub or Linear (grep confirms no gh issue edit, gh api -X POST/PATCH, or mutation)
model-tiers.json contains pick, and the existing registration test still passes with pick_buckets present in repo-policy.json
tasks.summary: Added the /pick skill (GitHub path) with resolve-repo, pick-fetch-gh, validate-candidates and rank-render scripts, SpawnedSapien pick_buckets, a pick entry in model-tiers.json, and a fixture smoke test. The smoke test passes 14 of 14 and includes the existing standup registration test.

tasks.title: Linear fetch and Quaestor-Web buckets
tasks.description: Add scripts/pick/pick-fetch-linear.sh using Linear GraphQL via LINEAR_API_KEY, same approach as scripts/standup/fetch-linear-standup.sh. Resolves 'me' to the user's Linear user id and applies a Linear IssueFilter JSON object per bucket. Emits the same normalized candidate JSON shape as pick-fetch-gh.sh, including points, state, project, parent, assignee, gitBranchName, blockedBy relations with blocker state and linked PRs. First step: run one read-only GraphQL query to verify the 'Ready to Assign' and 'Backlog' workflow state names and the Keystone team key, and record the verified values. Add pick_buckets to the Quaestor-Web entry: my-sprint (assignee me, active cycle, state not completed or canceled, no focus) and unclaimed (team Keystone, unassigned, state Ready to Assign or Backlog, focus shown). User-facing wording says 'sprint', never 'cycle'. Start line uses Linear gitBranchName.
acceptance_criteria: Verified Linear state names and Keystone team key are recorded in the bucket definitions, taken from a live read-only query
pick-fetch-linear.sh against a recorded GraphQL fixture emits candidate JSON identical in shape to the gh script output, checked by a smoke script
Bare /pick in Quaestor-Web shows exactly my-sprint and unclaimed in the menu and renders a top-5 list with 'wt <gitBranchName>  ->  /grill-me <ID>' start lines
No Linear mutation appears in the script
tasks.summary: Added pick-fetch-linear.sh (read-only Linear GraphQL, '@me' resolved via viewer, emits the gh candidate shape plus a 'prs' key) and Quaestor-Web my-sprint and unclaimed buckets. Live-verified team key KEY (Keystone) and states 'Ready to Assign' and 'Backlog' and recorded them under pick_verified in repo-policy.json. Smoke test 23/23.

tasks.title: pick-scorer agent and effort scoring
tasks.description: Add a Sonnet agent pick-scorer with a fixed JSON input/output contract (candidates in, per-candidate effort score plus one-line reason out) so /improve-agent-benchmarks can tune it later. Rubric covers points, frontend vs backend, review complexity, target repo, and how clearly the ticket is scoped. The skill pre-sorts each bucket on tracker fields to the top 25, calls pick-scorer, and renders the reason on a 'why:' line per item. In unclaimed, Ready to Assign vs Backlog is a soft penalty and unpointed tickets show '⚠ unpointed' but can still rank high if clearly tiny. Register pick-scorer in agents/registry.json with consumer pick.
acceptance_criteria: pick-scorer returns schema-valid JSON for a fixture of 25 candidates, each with a score and a one-line reason, checked by a validation script
Pre-sort caps scorer input at 25 candidates regardless of bucket size
An unpointed fixture ticket renders with '⚠ unpointed' and is not hard-excluded
agents/registry.json lists pick-scorer and the contract file exists next to the agent
tasks.summary: Added the pick-scorer Sonnet agent with a JSON contract, validate-scorer.py, the 25-candidate cap and score re-rank with 'why:' lines and '⚠ unpointed' in rank-render.py. Registered pick-scorer in agents/registry.json and model-tiers.json (T2). Merge conflict with T-0029 in test-pick.sh and SKILL.md resolved by hand (additive). Combined smoke test 30/30.

tasks.title: Blocker tiers and stackable start lines
tasks.description: Classify each candidate as ready (no blockers or all blockers merged/Done), stackable (every open blocker has a PR in review), or blocked (any blocker not started or in progress with no PR). Rank ready first, then stackable; hide blocked and print the hidden count. Linear uses native blockedBy relations with blocker state and linked PRs. GitHub uses native issue dependencies with 'blocked by #N' body text as fallback. Stackable items show the blocker's branch and the start line passes it as the second positional arg: 'wt <branch> <base>'. Whether a bucket hides blocked tickets is driven by its sort array (hide-blocked) so each repo config decides; the seed left tiers for unclaimed and SpawnedSapien open, so default hide-blocked on for all four SpawnedSapien buckets and my-sprint, and apply tiers to unclaimed as well.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture with one ready, one stackable, and one blocked ticket renders ready first, stackable second with a base branch in its start line, and the blocked one hidden with 'N blocked' shown
GitHub fixture with 'blocked by #N' in the body is classified the same as a native dependency
Stackable start line has the form 'wt <branch> <blocker-branch>' with base as the second positional arg and no --base flag
tasks.summary: Added blockers.py (ready/stackable/blocked tiers, GitHub native-dependency plus 'blocked by #N' resolve) hooked into rank-render.py. Ready then stackable, blocked hidden with a count; stackable start lines are 'wt <branch> <base>'. Linear fetch now emits blocker branches. Smoke 9/9.

tasks.title: Teammate overlap rules
tasks.description: Hard-exclude any ticket whose parent/epic has a teammate with active sibling tickets. For project-level overlap, add a neutral annotation '👥 <name> active in <project>' that does not change rank. Applies to Linear candidates using parent, project, and assignee fields from the fetch script.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture where a teammate has an active sibling under the same parent excludes that ticket from the list
Fixture with project-level overlap only keeps the ticket's rank unchanged and adds the 👥 annotation
Overlap logic is shared filter code, not duplicated per bucket
tasks.summary: Added overlap.py (hard-exclude on parent-level teammate overlap, neutral '👥' annotation on project overlap) and read-only pick-fetch-linear-activity.sh, wired via rank-render.py --activity. Smoke 5/5. Activity query verified by fixture only, not live. Render conflict with T-0031 resolved by hand.

tasks.title: Focus menu for shared-pool buckets
tasks.description: For buckets flagged as shared-pool (unclaimed), ask 'Focus?' each run. Options are built live from projects in the user's own current sprint work, plus 'No focus' and free-text 'Other'. Focus is a ranking boost, not a filter, and the menu header shows the active focus. Not asked for my-sprint or any SpawnedSapien bucket. No stored or dated focus config.
acceptance_criteria: unclaimed run asks for focus with options derived from the user's current sprint projects plus 'No focus'
Choosing a focus project moves a matching fixture ticket up without removing non-matching tickets
my-sprint and SpawnedSapien buckets never prompt for focus
No focus value is written to disk
tasks.summary: Added focus-options.sh (live options from my-sprint projects plus 'No focus') and focus_boost.py, wired via rank-render.py --focus. Boost only, never filters, nothing saved. Smoke 12/12. Flag-parsing conflict resolved by hand.

tasks.title: Free-text bucket mapping and other-repos section
tasks.description: Free text after /pick (e.g. '/pick quick wins') is mapped to a bucket by plain-English match and skips the menu. Tickets whose code lives in a different repo than the current one are not filtered out. They render in a separate 'other repos' section below the main list, tagged with the target repo. Main list shows top 5, other-repos section shows up to 3.
acceptance_criteria: '/pick quick wins' in Quaestor-Web selects unclaimed without showing the menu
Fixture with 8 candidates, 4 of them in another repo, renders 5 main items max and at most 3 under 'other repos' with repo tags
Unmatched free text falls back to the bucket menu
tasks.summary: Added map-bucket.py (free text to bucket via aliases, exit 1 falls back to menu) and sections.py (other-repos section, up to 3 tagged items). Quaestor-Web unclaimed got aliases incl. 'quick wins'. Smoke 7/7. Render conflict resolved by hand; SKILL.md overlap step made required.

tasks.title: Pipeline registration and final checks
tasks.description: Add skill-pipeline.json edge pick -> grill-me with when 'ticket chosen, start a new session and grill it'. Confirm the standard learning-capture tail with slug pick is present and consistent with the injector. Verify against Claude Code docs that disable-model-invocation: true is a supported skill frontmatter field, and fall back to the supported mechanism if not. Extend or add a registration smoke script covering pick in model-tiers.json, pick-scorer in agents/registry.json, the pipeline edge, and pick_buckets in repo-policy.json.
acceptance_criteria: Registration smoke script passes for pick, pick-scorer, pipeline edge, and pick_buckets
inject-learning-tail.py validates every slug in the pick edge as an existing skill directory
disable-model-invocation behavior is confirmed against docs and recorded in the task summary
tasks.summary: Added pick -> grill-me pipeline edge (baked into pick tail), pick in learning-contract producers and benchmark PLAN_CMDS, and test-pick-registration.sh. disable-model-invocation: true confirmed supported per code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md (blocks auto-invocation, /pick still works). Tier already consistent (T1 haiku/low). Injector check scoped to pick edge slugs after ignored skills/synced/ dir caused a local false failure. All pick smoke scripts pass (76).
